rationale: Chapter-heading phrase: ⲥⲁϣϩ (Lyc. seven, = Sah. ⲥⲁϣϥ̄/ⲥⲁϣϥⲉ) + ⲛⲍⲱⲃ ('of works,' from ϩⲱⲃ in vocab). Standard Manichaean enumeration formula introducing the seven cosmogonic acts of the Living Spirit.

proposed_english: the one clothed (= the suffering Jesus)
rationale: Relative perfect substantive: 'he who has been clothed/covered.' From ⲃⲱϭⲥ 'clothe, cover.' Technical Manichaean designation of the Jesus patibilis — the cosmic suffering Jesus enrobed in matter, here paired with ⲣⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲉ 'crucify' to identify the bound-and-spread savior figure of the Cross of Light.

Greek πύργος / πυργίσκος 'tower / small tower.' Cosmological structure (likely the cosmic watchtower/turret of the soul-fashioning apparatus); appears in line 13 as the manner-comparison for the place to which the soul is restored.

Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ (Lyc. for ϭⲗⲟⲡⲉ 'deceit, secret thing'). Cosmological locus of cosmic falsehood; the three living words are dispatched against three such places in the sixth work of the Living Spirit.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲙⲥ̄ 'submerge, plunge, drown.' Used here of the descent inward to find the soul scattered in matter. Distinct from ⲱⲙϩ 'embrace' though sometimes confused.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲗⲱϫϩ̄ 'defile, pollute' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲍ for ϩ pattern). Used in line 17 of the soul defiled in/by the Enemy.
Lycopolitan ⲁϥ-ⲕⲧⲟ-ϥ 'he turned him' (Sah. ⲕⲧⲟ 'turn, return') with object suffix. Standard verb of restoration/return; here the agent turns the redeemed one back to his proper cosmic place.

Lycopolitan nominalization of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer, respond' (with ⲍ for ϣ). Distinct from ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'the Hearing/Answer' in accumulated vocab — this form appears to designate the act of answering itself rather than the cosmic Hearing-figure. Line 18 has the soul stand 'at the answering, in the icon of the Father.'
